item.text: The current file is cleaner than the original, but it still mixes algorithm, formatting, and demo behavior in one type. I’m splitting those responsibilities into a small reusable sort class plus a minimal demo entry point.
I’m turning this into two source files: one focused sort utility and one demo runner. That makes the algorithm class reusable and removes the sample/output concerns from it.

The utility is now stripped down to sorting and display formatting. I’m adding a small `BubbleSortDemo` entry point so the executable example remains intact without forcing `main` to live in the algorithm class.
One more cleanup before verification: the demo is copying the sample array before calling `sortedCopy`, which already clones its input. I’m removing that redundant copy and then compiling both files.
The demo no longer needs `Arrays`, so I’m dropping that import and then running a full compile/execute check on the new entry point.

Refactored the code into a cleaner two-file shape. [BubbleSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/test_subject/bubble_sort_Java/BubbleSort.java) is now just the reusable utility API, and [BubbleSortDemo.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/test_subject/bubble_sort_Java/BubbleSortDemo.java) owns the sample data and console output.
